Chunk 1: DBMS Definition 
Definition: 
A Database Management System (DBMS) is software that manages databases and 
provides an interface to store, retrieve, and manipulate data. 
Explanation: 
It acts as a bridge between users/applications and the database, ensuring data is 
organized and accessible. 
Key Points: 
• Manages structured data  
• Provides data security and integrity  
• Supports multiple users  
Example: 
MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL 
Interview Tip: 
Mention “data management + interface + security” .

Chunk 2: Database 
Definition: 
A database is an organized collection of related data. 
Explanation: 
Data is stored in structured form for easy access and management. 
Key Points: 
• Stored electronically  
• Organized into tables  
• Easily retrievable  
Example: 
Student records database 
Interview Tip: 
Database = data, DBMS = software.

Chunk 3: Types of DBMS 
Definition: 
Different models of organizing data. 
Explanation: 
Each model defines how data is stored and accessed. 
Key Points: 
• Hierarchical  
• Network  
• Relational  
• NoSQL  
Example: 
Relational → MySQL 
Interview Tip: 
Relational DBMS is most widely used.

Chunk 4: Relational Model 
Definition: 
Data is stored in tables (relations). 
Explanation: 
Tables consist of rows and columns with relationships. 
Key Points: 
• Row → Tuple  
• Column → Attribute  
• Table → Relation  
Example: 
Student(ID, Name) 
Interview Tip: 
Primary key uniquely identifies row.

Chunk 5: Keys in DBMS 
Definition: 
Attributes used to identify records. 
Explanation: 
Keys ensure uniqueness and relationships. 
Key Points: 
• Primary Key  
• Foreign Key  
• Candidate Key  
• Super Key  
Example: 
StudentID as Primary Key 
Interview Tip: 
Primary key = unique + not null.

Chunk 6: ER Model 
Definition: 
Entity-Relationship model represents data logically. 
Explanation: 
Used for database design before implementation. 
Key Points: 
• Entity  
• Attribute  
• Relationship  
Example: 
Student — enrolls — Course 
Interview Tip: 
ER diagram is frequently asked.

Chunk 7: Normalization 
Definition: 
Process of organizing data to reduce redundancy. 
Explanation: 
Breaks tables into smaller ones. 
Key Points: 
• 1NF , 2NF , 3NF  
• Removes anomalies  
Example: 
Separate student and course tables 
Interview Tip: 
3NF is most commonly used.

Chunk 8: Functional Dependency 
Definition: 
Relationship between attributes. 
Explanation: 
One attribute determines another. 
Key Points: 
• X → Y  
• Used in normalization  
Example: 
ID → Name 
Interview Tip: 
Basis for normalization.

Chunk 9: SQL Basics 
Definition: 
Structured Query Language for DB operations. 
Explanation: 
Used to interact with databases. 
Key Points: 
• DDL  
• DML  
• DCL  
• TCL  
Example: 
SELECT * FROM Students; 
Interview Tip: 
SQL is case-insensitive.

Chunk 10: DDL Commands 
Definition: 
Data Definition Language commands. 
Explanation: 
Used to define database structure. 
Key Points: 
• CREATE  
• ALTER  
• DROP  
Example: 
CREATE TABLE Student(...); 
Interview Tip: 
DDL changes schema.

Chunk 11: DML Commands 
Definition: 
Data Manipulation Language commands. 
Explanation: 
Used to manipulate data. 
Key Points: 
• INSERT  
• UPDATE  
• DELETE  
Example: 
INSERT INTO Student VALUES(...); 
Interview Tip: 
DML modifies data only.

Chunk 12: Joins in SQL 
Definition: 
Combine data from multiple tables. 
Explanation: 
Used when data is distributed across tables. 
Key Points: 
• INNER JOIN  
• LEFT JOIN  
• RIGHT JOIN  
• FULL JOIN  
Example: 
Student JOIN Course 
Interview Tip: 
INNER JOIN is most common.

Chunk 13: Transactions 
Definition: 
A sequence of operations as a single unit. 
Explanation: 
Ensures data consistency. 
Key Points: 
• Commit  
• Rollback  
Example: 
Bank transfer 
Interview Tip: 
Transaction must be atomic.

Chunk 14: ACID Properties 
Definition: 
Properties ensuring reliable transactions. 
Explanation: 
Guarantees correctness of DB operations. 
Key Points: 
• Atomicity  
• Consistency  
• Isolation  
• Durability  
Example: 
Money transfer consistency 
Interview Tip: 
Very frequently asked question.

Chunk 15: Indexing 
Definition: 
Technique to speed up data retrieval. 
Explanation: 
Works like a book index. 
Key Points: 
• Improves search speed  
• Uses extra memory  
Example: 
Index on StudentID 
Interview Tip: 
Trade-off: speed vs space.

Chunk 16: Views 
Definition: 
Virtual tables. 
Explanation: 
Do not store data physically. 
Key Points: 
• Derived from queries  
• Improves security  
Example: 
View of selected columns 
Interview Tip: 
Views don’t store actual data.

Chunk 17: Stored Procedures 
Definition: 
Predefined SQL code stored in DB. 
Explanation: 
Reusable and efficient. 
Key Points: 
• Improves performance  
• Reduces redundancy  
Example: 
Procedure for inserting data 
Interview Tip: 
Used in enterprise systems.

Chunk 18: Triggers 
Definition: 
Automatically executed actions. 
Explanation: 
Triggered by events like insert/update. 
Key Points: 
• BEFORE/AFTER triggers  
• Used for validation  
Example: 
Audit logs 
Interview Tip: 
Trigger runs automatically.

Chunk 19: Concurrency Control 
Definition: 
Managing multiple transactions. 
Explanation: 
Prevents conflicts. 
Key Points: 
• Locking  
• Timestamping  
Example: 
Two users editing same data 
Interview Tip: 
Avoids data inconsistency.

Chunk 20: Deadlock in DBMS 
Definition: 
Transactions waiting indefinitely. 
Explanation: 
Occurs due to resource locking. 
Key Points: 
• Circular wait  
• Detection required  
Example: 
T1 waits for T2, T2 waits for T1 
Interview Tip: 
Similar to OS deadlock.

Chunk 21: NoSQL Databases 
Definition: 
Non-relational databases. 
Explanation: 
Used for unstructured data. 
Key Points: 
• Key-value  
• Document  
• Column-based  
Example: 
MongoDB 
Interview Tip: 
Used in big data systems.

Chunk : Interview Questions 
1. What is DBMS? 
Software to manage databases. 
2. DBMS vs File System? 
DBMS provides security and consistency. 
3. What is normalization? 
Reducing redundancy. 
4. What is a key? 
Attribute to identify records. 
5. Types of keys? 
Primary, Foreign, Candidate. 
6. What is SQL? 
Query language for DB. 
7. What are joins? 
Combining tables. 
8. What is ACID? 
Transaction properties. 
9. What is a transaction? 
Unit of work. 
10. What is indexing? 
Faster data retrieval. 
11. What is a view? 
Virtual table. 
12. What is a trigger? 
Auto-executed action. 
13. What is deadlock? 
Transactions stuck waiting. 
14. What is concurrency control? 
Managing multiple transactions. 
15. What is functional dependency? 
Relation between attributes. 
16. What is ER model? 
Logical DB design. 
17. What is DDL? 
Schema definition. 
18. What is DML? 
Data manipulation. 
19. What is NoSQL? 
Non-relational DB. 
20. What is stored procedure? 
Reusable SQL code.

Chunk 1: Operating System Definition 
Definition: 
An Operating System (OS) is system software that manages hardware and software 
resources and provides services to programs. 
Explanation: 
It acts as a bridge between user and hardware. Without OS, users must interact directly 
with hardware, which is complex. 
Key Points: 
• Interface between user and hardware  
• Manages CPU, memory, files, devices  
• Provides execution environment  
Example: 
Windows, Linux, macOS 
Interview Tip: 
Always mention “resource management + interface” in definition.

Chunk 2: Functions of OS 
Definition: 
Core responsibilities performed by the OS. 
Explanation: 
OS ensures efficient and safe use of system resources. 
Key Points: 
• Process management  
• Memory management  
• File system management  
• Device management  
• Security  
Example: 
OS allocates CPU to running apps. 
Interview Tip: 
List at least 4 functions when asked.

Chunk 3: Types of Operating Systems 
Definition: 
Different categories based on functionality. 
Explanation: 
Each type is designed for specific use cases. 
Key Points: 
• Batch OS  
• Time-sharing OS  
• Distributed OS  
• Real-time OS  
• Multiprocessing OS  
Example: 
Real-time OS in embedded systems 
Interview Tip: 
RTOS = strict timing constraints.

Chunk 4: Process 
Definition: 
A process is a program in execution. 
Explanation: 
It includes code, data, stack, registers, and resources. 
Key Points: 
• Active entity  
• Has state  
• Requires resources  
Example: 
Running Chrome browser 
Interview Tip: 
Program = passive, Process = active.

Chunk 5: Process States 
Definition: 
Different stages of a process lifecycle. 
Explanation: 
Processes move between states during execution. 
Key Points: 
• New  
• Ready  
• Running  
• Waiting  
• Terminated  
Example: 
Waiting state → I/O operation 
Interview Tip: 
Draw state diagram if asked.

Chunk 6: Process Scheduling 
Definition: 
Selection of process for CPU execution. 
Explanation: 
Scheduler decides which process runs next. 
Key Points: 
• CPU utilization  
• Throughput  
• Turnaround time  
• Waiting time  
Example: 
OS selects process from ready queue 
Interview Tip: 
Focus on performance metrics.

Chunk 7: Scheduling Algorithms 
Definition: 
Methods used to schedule processes. 
Explanation: 
Each algorithm has pros and cons. 
Key Points: 
• FCFS  
• SJF  
• Round Robin  
• Priority Scheduling  
Example: 
Round Robin → time slice based 
Interview Tip: 
SJF gives minimum average waiting time.

Chunk 8: Threads 
Definition: 
Smallest unit of CPU execution. 
Explanation: 
Threads share process resources. 
Key Points: 
• Lightweight  
• Faster than processes  
• Shared memory  
Example: 
Multiple threads in a browser tab 
Interview Tip: 
Thread vs Process is very common question.

Chunk 9: Process vs Thread 
Definition: 
Comparison between process and thread. 
Explanation: 
Processes are independent, threads are not. 
Key Points: 
• Process → heavy  
• Thread → lightweight  
• Process → separate memory  
• Thread → shared memory  
Example: 
Multiple threads inside one process 
Interview Tip: 
Mention memory sharing difference.

Chunk 10: Inter-Process Communication (IPC) 
Definition: 
Mechanism for processes to communicate. 
Explanation: 
Processes need IPC for coordination. 
Key Points: 
• Shared memory  
• Message passing  
Example: 
Pipes in Linux 
Interview Tip: 
Shared memory is faster than message passing.

Chunk 11: Deadlock 
Definition: 
A state where processes wait forever. 
Explanation: 
Occurs due to resource contention. 
Key Points: 
• Mutual exclusion  
• Hold and wait  
• No preemption  
• Circular wait  
Example: 
Two processes waiting on each other 
Interview Tip: 
All 4 conditions must occur.

Chunk 12: Deadlock Handling 
Definition: 
Methods to manage deadlocks. 
Explanation: 
OS prevents or resolves deadlocks. 
Key Points: 
• Prevention  
• Avoidance  
• Detection  
• Recovery  
Example: 
Banker’s Algorithm 
Interview Tip: 
Avoidance = safe state concept.

Chunk 13: Memory Management 
Definition: 
Managing main memory efficiently. 
Explanation: 
OS allocates and frees memory. 
Key Points: 
• Allocation  
• Deallocation  
• Protection  
Example: 
RAM allocation to processes 
Interview Tip: 
Fragmentation is important concept.

Chunk 14: Paging 
Definition: 
Memory management using fixed-size blocks. 
Explanation: 
Logical memory divided into pages. 
Key Points: 
• Page table  
• No external fragmentation  
Example: 
Virtual memory systems 
Interview Tip: 
Internal fragmentation may occur.

Chunk 15: Segmentation 
Definition: 
Memory divided into variable-sized segments. 
Explanation: 
Based on logical divisions. 
Key Points: 
• Code, data, stack segments  
• External fragmentation  
Example: 
Separate code and data segments 
Interview Tip: 
Segmentation is user-visible.

Chunk 16: Virtual Memory 
Definition: 
Technique to use disk as memory. 
Explanation: 
Allows execution of large programs. 
Key Points: 
• Demand paging  
• Page fault  
Example: 
Swapping pages from disk 
Interview Tip: 
Virtual memory improves multitasking.

Chunk 17: File System 
Definition: 
Structure for storing data. 
Explanation: 
OS organizes files and directories. 
Key Points: 
• File creation  
• Deletion  
• Access control  
Example: 
NTFS, EXT4 
Interview Tip: 
Know file allocation methods.

Chunk 18: Disk Scheduling 
Definition: 
Order of disk access requests. 
Explanation: 
Improves performance. 
Key Points: 
• FCFS  
• SSTF  
• SCAN  
Example: 
Elevator algorithm (SCAN) 
Interview Tip: 
SCAN reduces seek time.

Chunk 19: System Calls 
Definition: 
Interface between user and OS. 
Explanation: 
Programs request OS services. 
Key Points: 
• Process control  
• File management  
• Device control  
Example: 
open(), read() 
Interview Tip: 
System calls = OS API.

Chunk 20: Kernel 
Definition: 
Core part of OS. 
Explanation: 
Handles low-level operations. 
Key Points: 
• Process scheduling  
• Memory management  
Example: 
Linux kernel 
Interview Tip: 
Kernel runs in privileged mode.

Chunk 21: User Mode vs Kernel Mode 
Definition: 
Two execution modes. 
Explanation: 
Ensures security. 
Key Points: 
• User mode → limited access  
• Kernel mode → full access  
Example: 
System call switches mode 
Interview Tip: 
Mode switch is important concept.

Chunk : Interview Questions 
1. What is OS? 
Manages hardware and provides services. 
2. Process vs Thread? 
Process = independent, Thread = lightweight. 
3. What is Deadlock? 
Processes waiting forever. 
4. Conditions of Deadlock? 
4 necessary conditions. 
5. What is Scheduling? 
CPU allocation process. 
6. Best scheduling algorithm? 
Depends on use-case (SJF optimal). 
7. What is Paging? 
Fixed-size memory allocation. 
8. Paging vs Segmentation? 
Fixed vs variable size. 
9. What is Virtual Memory? 
Disk used as RAM. 
10. What is IPC? 
Process communication methods. 
11. What is Kernel? 
Core OS component. 
12. System call example? 
read(), write() 
13. What is context switching? 
Switching CPU between processes. 
14. What is fragmentation? 
Wasted memory space. 
15. Internal vs External fragmentation? 
Inside vs outside blocks. 
16. What is thrashing? 
Excessive paging. 
17. What is semaphore? 
Synchronization tool. 
18. What is mutex? 
Mutual exclusion lock. 
19. What is file system? 
Data organization method. 
20. What is RTOS? 
Time-critical OS.

Definition: 
Spring Boot is an open-source Java framework built on top of the Spring Framework 
that simplifies backend development using auto-configuration and embedded 
servers. 
Key Features: 
 Auto-configuration  
 Embedded server (Tomcat)  
 Starter dependencies  
 Minimal configuration  
Use Case: 
Used to build REST APIs and microservices quickly. 
 
🔹

Title: Advantages of Spring Boot 
Benefits: 
 Faster development  
 Less boilerplate code  
 Easy deployment (JAR file)  
 Built-in production tools  
 
🔹

Title: Spring Boot Project Structure 
Components: 
 Controller → handles HTTP  
 Service → business logic  
 Repository → database  
 Model → entity  
 DTO → data transfer

 Easier testing

 PUT → update

Chunk 8: JPA

JPA is a Java specification for database operations. 
Implementation: 
Hibernate 
 
🔹

Chunk 9: Repository Layer 
Title: Spring Data Repository

Handles database operations. 
Example: 
public interface UserRepo extends JpaRepository<User, Long> {}

Chunk 10: Service Layer

Contains business logic.

Chunk 11: Controller Layer

Handles HTTP requests and responses.

Chunk 12: DTO Pattern

Used to transfer data between layers.

 Security  
 Clean API

Chunk 13: Validation

Validates user input using annotations. 
Examples: 
 @NotNull  
 @Email  
 @Size  
 
🔹

Chunk 14: Exception Handling 
Title: Global Exception Handling 
Definition: 
Handles errors using @ControllerAdvice. 
 
🔹

Chunk 15: Spring Security 
Title: Spring Security 
Definition: 
Framework for authentication and authorization.

Chunk 16: JWT 
Title: JWT Authentication

Token-based authentication. 
Structure: 
Header.Payload.Signature

Chunk 17: JWT Flow

Steps:

3. Client sends token

 Integration test

• Time-sharing OS  
• Distributed OS  
• Real-time OS  
• Multiprocessing OS  
Example: 
Real-time OS in embedded systems 
Interview Tip: 
RTOS = strict timing constraints.

Chunk 4: Process 
Definition: 
A process is a program in execution. 
Explanation: 
It includes code, data, stack, registers, and resources. 
Key Points: 
• Active entity  
• Has state  
• Requires resources  
Example: 
Running Chrome browser 
Interview Tip: 
Program = passive, Process = active.

Chunk 5: Process States 
Definition: 
Different stages of a process lifecycle. 
Explanation: 
Processes move between states during execution. 
Key Points: 
• New  
• Ready  
• Running  
• Waiting  
• Terminated  
Example: 
Waiting state → I/O operation 
Interview Tip: 
Draw state diagram if asked.

Chunk 6: Process Scheduling 
Definition: 
Selection of process for CPU execution. 
Explanation: 
Scheduler decides which process runs next. 
Key Points: 
• CPU utilization  
• Throughput  
• Turnaround time  
• Waiting time  
Example: 
OS selects process from ready queue 
Interview Tip: 
Focus on performance metrics.

Chunk 7: Scheduling Algorithms 
Definition: 
Methods used to schedule processes. 
Explanation: 
Each algorithm has pros and cons. 
Key Points: 
• FCFS  
• SJF  
• Round Robin  
• Priority Scheduling  
Example: 
Round Robin → time slice based 
Interview Tip: 
SJF gives minimum average waiting time.

Chunk 8: Threads 
Definition: 
Smallest unit of CPU execution. 
Explanation: 
Threads share process resources. 
Key Points: 
• Lightweight  
• Faster than processes  
• Shared memory  
Example: 
Multiple threads in a browser tab 
Interview Tip: 
Thread vs Process is very common question.

Chunk 9: Process vs Thread 
Definition: 
Comparison between process and thread. 
Explanation: 
Processes are independent, threads are not. 
Key Points: 
• Process → heavy  
• Thread → lightweight  
• Process → separate memory  
• Thread → shared memory  
Example: 
Multiple threads inside one process 
Interview Tip: 
Mention memory sharing difference.

Chunk 10: Inter-Process Communication (IPC) 
Definition: 
Mechanism for processes to communicate. 
Explanation: 
Processes need IPC for coordination. 
Key Points: 
• Shared memory  
• Message passing  
Example: 
Pipes in Linux 
Interview Tip: 
Shared memory is faster than message passing.

Chunk 11: Deadlock 
Definition: 
A state where processes wait forever. 
Explanation: 
Occurs due to resource contention. 
Key Points: 
• Mutual exclusion  
• Hold and wait  
• No preemption  
• Circular wait  
Example: 
Two processes waiting on each other 
Interview Tip: 
All 4 conditions must occur.

Chunk 12: Deadlock Handling 
Definition: 
Methods to manage deadlocks. 
Explanation: 
OS prevents or resolves deadlocks. 
Key Points: 
• Prevention  
• Avoidance  
• Detection  
• Recovery  
Example: 
Banker’s Algorithm 
Interview Tip: 
Avoidance = safe state concept.

Chunk 13: Memory Management 
Definition: 
Managing main memory efficiently. 
Explanation: 
OS allocates and frees memory. 
Key Points: 
• Allocation  
• Deallocation  
• Protection  
Example: 
RAM allocation to processes 
Interview Tip: 
Fragmentation is important concept.

Chunk 14: Paging 
Definition: 
Memory management using fixed-size blocks. 
Explanation: 
Logical memory divided into pages. 
Key Points: 
• Page table  
• No external fragmentation  
Example: 
Virtual memory systems 
Interview Tip: 
Internal fragmentation may occur.

Chunk 15: Segmentation 
Definition: 
Memory divided into variable-sized segments. 
Explanation: 
Based on logical divisions. 
Key Points: 
• Code, data, stack segments  
• External fragmentation  
Example: 
Separate code and data segments 
Interview Tip: 
Segmentation is user-visible.

Chunk 16: Virtual Memory 
Definition: 
Technique to use disk as memory. 
Explanation: 
Allows execution of large programs. 
Key Points: 
• Demand paging  
• Page fault  
Example: 
Swapping pages from disk 
Interview Tip: 
Virtual memory improves multitasking.

Chunk 17: File System 
Definition: 
Structure for storing data. 
Explanation: 
OS organizes files and directories. 
Key Points: 
• File creation  
• Deletion  
• Access control  
Example: 
NTFS, EXT4 
Interview Tip: 
Know file allocation methods.

Chunk 18: Disk Scheduling 
Definition: 
Order of disk access requests. 
Explanation: 
Improves performance. 
Key Points: 
• FCFS  
• SSTF  
• SCAN  
Example: 
Elevator algorithm (SCAN) 
Interview Tip: 
SCAN reduces seek time.

Chunk 19: System Calls 
Definition: 
Interface between user and OS. 
Explanation: 
Programs request OS services. 
Key Points: 
• Process control  
• File management  
• Device control  
Example: 
open(), read() 
Interview Tip: 
System calls = OS API.

Chunk 20: Kernel 
Definition: 
Core part of OS. 
Explanation: 
Handles low-level operations. 
Key Points: 
• Process scheduling  
• Memory management  
Example: 
Linux kernel 
Interview Tip: 
Kernel runs in privileged mode.

Chunk 21: User Mode vs Kernel Mode 
Definition: 
Two execution modes. 
Explanation: 
Ensures security. 
Key Points: 
• User mode → limited access  
• Kernel mode → full access  
Example: 
System call switches mode 
Interview Tip: 
Mode switch is important concept.
